children: Bank of America Securities clients poured record cash into mid-cap equities
stocks last week while dumping industrials
Overall, clients returned to buying U.S. equities following a week of de-risking, purchasing $1.3B in single stocks and $1.7B in exchange-traded funds, according to a recent BofA note.

Institutional investors led the buying spree, acting as net buyers for the third time in four weeks, while hedge funds also added to their positions. Retail clients, conversely, remained net sellers for an eighth consecutive week.
The flow data point to a sharp divergence in size and sector preferences. Clients rotated out of large-cap
equities to drive record inflows into mid-cap stocks, marking the fifth-largest week of mid-cap purchases since 2008 when normalized by market capitalization.
BofA strategist Jill Carey said he favors mid-caps over small-caps
for the second half of the year, citing lower interest rate risk alongside comparable earnings recovery profiles.
At the sector level, industrials experienced a historic capitulation, suffering their largest weekly outflows in BofA's data history dating back to 2008. In stark contrast, technology
and healthcare stocks absorbed the bulk of the buying, with healthcare seeing its second-largest week of inflows on record when normalized by market cap.
ETF activity largely mirrored these trends, with broad inflows recorded across all major styles and size segments, led by tech funds, while energy ETFs faced the heaviest outflows.

title: BofA clients resumed buying stocks last week after big de-risking
